past_medical_history: IgM monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) — diagnosed 2 years ago by hematology
family_history: No family history of neuropathy or blood disorders

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive bilateral distal leg and foot numbness with gait instability over 3 years — hematologist referred to neurology given IgM MGUS
patient.history_present_illness: A 68-year-old retired banker with IgM MGUS (IgM paraprotein 0.8 g/dL, diagnosed 2 years ago by hematology during a routine evaluation for mildly elevated total protein) presented to neurology clinic for evaluation of progressive bilateral foot and leg numbness and gait instability. He notes the onset of numbness was gradual over approximately three years — he initially noticed tingling and reduced sensation in both feet, which progressively worsened and is now at mid-calf level. He has become increasingly unsteady on his feet, particularly in the dark or on uneven surfaces, and has had two near-falls. He does not describe significant pain — the predominant symptom is numbness and profound unsteadiness. He has also noticed increasing difficulty with fine finger tasks — he struggles with small buttons and has difficulty feeling the keys on his keyboard. His wife notes that he has a distinctive wobbly gait with exaggerated arm movements for balance. His IgM MGUS was being followed with annual monitoring; hematology detected a slightly larger paraprotein (0.8 → 1.1 g/dL) on the most recent value 3 months ago and referred him to neurology given concern for paraprotein-associated neuropathy. He denies constitutional symptoms — no fever, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss.

neurological_exam.motor: Mild bilateral distal weakness — toe extension 4/5 bilaterally, ankle dorsiflexion 4+/5. Mild bilateral hand intrinsic weakness (grip 4+/5). Proximal strength normal.
neurological_exam.sensory: Severe proprioceptive loss bilateral great toes and ankles — cannot detect 1 cm movement. Vibration absent at great toes and ankles bilaterally. Reduced vibration at mid-calf. Light touch and pinprick — stocking pattern to knees, glove to wrists. Touch grossly preserved but proprioception disproportionately impaired.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Ankle reflexes absent. Knee jerks absent. Biceps and brachioradialis 1+. Triceps trace. Plantar flexors bilaterally.
neurological_exam.coordination: Heel-shin — marked sensory ataxia, unable to complete. Finger-nose: mild inaccuracy due to proprioceptive loss.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based sensory ataxia. Romberg markedly positive (falls within seconds of eye closure). Steppage component. Cannot tandem walk. Uses arms widely for balance.
neurological_exam.additional: No pes cavus. No organomegaly appreciated on brief inspection. No peripheral adenopathy.

Neuropathy_workup.value: IgM paraprotein 1.1 g/dL (increased from 0.8 g/dL 6 months ago)

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: SPEP IgM paraprotein 1.1 g/dL (increased from 0.8 g/dL 6 months ago) (H), Anti-MAG antibodies Positive — titer 1:102,400 (markedly elevated) (H), Immunofixation electrophoresis (IFE) IgM kappa monoclonal protein confirmed (H).
abnormal_values_summary: Anti-MAG antibodies positive 1: 102,400 (diagnostic for anti-MAG neuropathy) (H)

specialized_test.test_type: Nerve conduction studies and EMG — bilateral upper and lower extremities

findings.pattern: Markedly slow velocity — demyelinating; reduced amplitude
Reduced amplitude, markedly slow velocity — demyelinating; note: DML markedly prolonged 7.4 ms
Markedly slow velocity, prolonged DML — demyelinating
Markedly prolonged DML, slow velocity — predominantly distal/terminal slowing

quantitative_data.pattern: Predominantly demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy — markedly prolonged distal motor latencies and slow velocities, especially distally; predominant 'terminal slowing' pattern

specialized_test.impression: Demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy with disproportionately prolonged distal motor latencies. Distal motor latencies markedly prolonged (peroneal 8.6 ms, tibial 9.2 ms; reference <5 ms) with relatively preserved proximal conduction velocities — a pattern of predominantly distal/terminal demyelination. Sural and superficial peroneal SNAP amplitudes severely reduced with markedly slowed velocities. Median sensory also reduced in amplitude with slow velocity (DML 7.4 ms). Needle EMG shows rare fibrillations in tibialis anterior bilaterally with mildly chronic neurogenic motor unit morphology; no active denervation in gastrocnemius. Findings are consistent with a predominantly demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy with a distal-predominant pattern of conduction slowing

csf.interpretation: Albuminocytologic dissociation: elevated CSF protein with normal cell count. This pattern supports a demyelinating process rather than an axonal cause.

output.query: IgM MGUS anti-MAG neuropathy rituximab treatment outcomes

results.title: Anti-MAG neuropathy — rituximab treatment and outcomes
results.key_finding: Rituximab reduces anti-MAG antibody titers and stabilizes anti-MAG neuropathy in 40-50% of patients; improvement is partial and slow (6-12 months); early treatment associated with better outcomes

results.title: IgM MGUS progression to Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia
results.key_finding: IgM paraprotein >1.5 g/dL or increasing trend warrants bone marrow biopsy to exclude Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia; IgM 1.1 g/dL with increasing trend requires monitoring

output.test_type: Bone marrow biopsy with flow cytometry (hematology-performed)

findings.finding: Bone marrow cellularity 30% (normal for age). CD20+ B-cell clone detected — small lymphoplasmacytic population <5% of marrow cellularity. No evidence of Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia (requires >10% lymphoplasmacytic infiltration).
Flow cytometry: IgM kappa expressing B-cell clone confirmed; no high-grade lymphoma

output.impression: IgM MGUS — bone marrow biopsy shows lymphoplasmacytic infiltration below the threshold for Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia (<5% of marrow cellularity; diagnostic threshold >10%). IgM kappa monoclonal B-cell clone confirmed on flow cytometry. No evidence of high-grade lymphoma

output.test_type: Physical therapy evaluation and balance assessment

findings.finding: Berg Balance Scale: 32/56 (high fall risk — threshold <45)
Dynamic Gait Index: 12/24 (abnormal — high fall risk)
Severe proprioceptive loss — compensation strategies needed

output.impression: High fall risk on standardized balance assessment (Berg Balance Scale 32/56; Dynamic Gait Index 12/24). Findings consistent with severe proprioceptive loss contributing to postural instability and gait impairment

output.proposed: Neuropathic symptom management for anti-MAG neuropathy
warnings: Anti-MAG neuropathy is predominantly ataxic/proprioceptive — pain is less prominent than in diabetic neuropathy; balance rehabilitation is more important than pain medication
If neuropathic pain present: gabapentin or pregabalin reasonable

output.impression: Mild degenerative spine disease without significant cord compression or high-grade canal stenosis. No signal change in the cord to suggest myelopathy

output.query: anti-MAG neuropathy prognosis long-term outcome without treatment

results.title: Anti-MAG neuropathy — long-term natural history
results.key_finding: Anti-MAG neuropathy is typically slowly progressive; majority remain ambulatory at 10 years but with significant disability; rituximab can stabilize or partially improve in 40-50%

background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

mri.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No mass, haemorrhage, midline shift, or restricted diffusion. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus, or large-territory infarct.

differential.key_features: Demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy; differs by absence of IgM paraprotein and terminal slowing pattern; CIDP typically responds to IVIG.
Coexists with anti-MAG neuropathy; bone marrow biopsy with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate; MYD88 L265P mutation.
Onset usually in childhood; pes cavus, family history; genetic confirmation if suspected.
Axonal length-dependent; does not explain demyelinating + terminal slowing pattern with paraprotein.
Lambda monoclonal (vs IgM here); VEGF + osteosclerotic lesions absent.

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: SPEP / IFE / serum free light chains / quantitative immunoglobulins and anti-MAG antibody titer
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IgM monoclonal protein with high-titer anti-MAG IgM (Bühlmann ≥10,000 BTU) confirms anti-MAG neuropathy

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Albuminocytologic dissociation (elevated protein, normal cell count) supports CIDP

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm IgM MGUS or low-grade lymphoplasmacytic disease (Waldenström's) underlying anti-MAG neuropathy

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Send SPEP / IFE / serum free light chains AND anti-MAG titer in any chronic distal-predominant demyelinating neuropathy
Distinguish anti-MAG (terminal slowing) from CIDP (conduction block, temporal dispersion)
Hematology evaluation for IgM MGUS vs Waldenström's
Treatment: rituximab is first-line for symptomatic anti-MAG (typically poor response to IVIG)
contraindicated_actions: Do not use IVIG as first-line for anti-MAG (typically refractory)
Do not stop at 'CIDP' — anti-MAG is a distinct entity with different treatment
key_reasoning_points: Anti-MAG neuropathy: distal-predominant, demyelinating with terminal slowing, IgM kappa paraprotein
Up to 50% of patients with IgM MGUS-associated neuropathy have anti-MAG antibodies
Rituximab achieves partial response in many but disease modification is slow
